text:
morgan: Kicking off progressive release: canary v2.4.1-rc3 -> eu-west. Traffic target 10% in 5m windows. Change window until 23:00 UTC. Need ops/qa/infra ack for go.

sam: watching dashboards. I'll keep an eye on p95 and errors.

riley: quick Q — rollback plan ready?

morgan: yes. rollback command and pin snippets below. will also capture logs to s3.

morgan: rollback cmd:
```bash
redwood release rollback --service inference-api --to-version v2.4.0
```

morgan: pin version for callers if we need an emergency hold:
```bash
redwood config pin --route /v1/generate --version v2.4.0 --expires 10m
```

deploy-bot: :gear: release started: v2.4.1-rc3 -> eu-west (canary) | targets: 12 instances | traffic: 10% | initiated by morgan

lee: infra note — I'm warming up KV cache on the canary pool now, will verify hit rate in ~90s.

anya: seeing small 502 spike (0.8%) at +30s on one canary node, correlating with connection churn. posting logs to #incidents shortly.

sam: saw the 502 spike too, p95 latency up 120ms relative to baseline but still under SLO. I'd prefer hold until we validate retries.

riley: vote: hold — need more traces and stack for 502, also confirm k8s restarts count.

morgan: @infra-bot can you confirm pod restarts?

infra-bot: pod restarts: canary-pool-3 -> 1 restart in last 2m; host metrics normal.

lee: looks like ephemeral connection error from a pool node, not infra-wide. still recommend hold to investigate prefix cache behavior. :thinking_face: 

morgan: OK, hold at 10%. I’m pinning the route to current stable and pausing traffic shift.

morgan: pin command run:
```bash
redwood config pin --route /v1/generate --version v2.4.0 --reason "canary 502 spike" --expires 30m
```

deploy-bot: :no_entry: traffic shift paused by morgan. active canary traffic reverted to stable for callers pinned.

anya: pushing the error traces here: https://logs.redwood.internal/trace/xyz123 (short TTL)

sam: quick triage notes — 502s originate in decoder loop hitting a null pointer in our new batching path. Repro locally with seq_len > 1024.

riley: if reproducible locally that's a rollback for me. otherwise a targeted hotfix.

morgan: consensus seems to be rollback. I will trigger rollback and open a postmortem.

morgan: rollback cmd executed:
```bash
redwood release rollback --service inference-api --to-version v2.4.0 --reason "canary decoder NPEs" --notify oncall
```

deploy-bot: :repeat: rollback started by morgan -> target version v2.4.0. Rolling out to canary pool now. ETA 2m.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: rollback complete. All canary instances at v2.4.0, traffic restored to baseline.

lee: verified KV cache hit rates back to baseline, no pod restarts after rollback.

sam: QA confirms no 502s in the next 5m window. I'll move a list of failing prompts to the PR.

morgan: creating postmortem doc and linking in #postmortems. Also adding a preflight test for seq_len > 1024 to the CI.

riley: thanks all. for the record: re-run canary after fix with a deeper sampling (20% for 10m) and the prefix cache checks.

morgan: noted. closing this thread. :lock:
